edit.description: the walled-wave verdict case's order assertion over verdict.tags

summary: the walled-wave case asserts sequence over verdict.tags, which the spec defines as the tags provisioned, not an order

per.section: The tick verdict — one facts artifact

acceptance: the case asserts the provisioned tags order-free, and the posix lane stops reding at random on it
notes: The posix-lane red: `expected ['STAKE-B','STAKE-A'] to deeply equal ['STAKE-A','STAKE-B']` in the walled-wave verdict case. The sibling invocations assertion already sorts; verdict.tags does not. The spec promises "entry tags provisioned" and no order, and provisioned[] fills as slots refill, so the assertion reads a promise the engine never made. No tests[]: the whole diff is the file carrying the case, which rebuilds at the base by construction.
